event.description: Replace the 15x14 tied token table with a rank-5 learned token code and one shared learned 5-to-14 expansion used to form both input embeddings and output-logit rows, retaining all other current mechanisms.
event.proposal: Family: token representation. Retained incumbent is 3031 parameters at 99.990000%, a +0.990000 percentage-point margin over 99%. Same-family history: the most recent accepted token-representation result is attempt-0034, reversed padded operands (3129, 99.19%), while the most recent failed result is attempt-0033, reversed operands with one layer, an optimization failure peaking at 2.4% validation; 3 prior token-representation attempts. The immediately preceding affine-free-normalization attempt-0042 is an optimization failure (45000 steps, 8.3% peak validation, no checkpoint), not a scored nonqualification. Hypothesis: the vocabulary's 15 token identities may lie in a five-dimensional learned subspace when a shared learned expansion forms both the token input table and tied output-logit table; unlike the prior fixed rank-4 token basis, this preserves an adaptable token subspace. This is a representational token factorization, not parameterization-preserving scalar pruning, reducing actual parameters from 3031 to 2966. It is more informative than the nearest untested rank-4 learned factorization because rank 5 is the smallest reduction that retains a comparatively rich learned token subspace after the fixed rank-4 failure.
